title: Designing Operational Excellence and Automation
objective: Can connect IaC, change management, observability, and automated remediation with permissions, approvals, validation, and rollback.

prerequisites.title: Designing Resilience, Migration, and Business Continuity

sections.title: Reproducing Configurations with Code and Policies
paragraphs: With Infrastructure as Code, infrastructure is managed as declarations or instructions and applied in changes that can be reviewed. Storing templates alone does not provide reproducibility unless manual changes, secrets, organization-specific differences, and dependencies can also be managed.

For multi-account, multi-Region deployments, separate the shared foundation from workload-specific settings, and verify the execution role, Regions, stack dependencies, change impact, and drift. Encode policies as code and validate them in advance to stop violations before applying them in production.

sources.label: SAP-C03 Exam Guide: Infrastructure as Code

sections.title: Deliver and validate changes incrementally
paragraphs: A delivery pipeline must do more than automate builds and deployments. It must track the source, artifacts, dependencies, security checks, approvals, environment promotions, and execution roles so that you can explain which changes were released to which environments.

For production changes, observe quality, latency, error rates, and security-check results within a limited scope, and roll out the changes according to the criteria for continuing or stopping. If an anomaly occurs, revert to known-good artifacts and configuration, confirm the cause, and then retry.

sources.label: SAP-C03 Exam Guide: CI/CD and DevSecOps

sections.title: From Observability to Safe Remediation
paragraphs: Operations teams correlate request volume representing user impact, latency, and error rate with resource saturation, logs, traces, and configuration changes on the same timeline. They do not determine the cause from CPU utilization alone; they validate hypotheses by considering the target operation, dependencies, start time, deployments, and configuration changes.

Automated remediation must define the target, preconditions, a least-privilege execution role, success conditions, stop conditions, and rollback. Do not treat the occurrence of an alarm as the cause and change all environments at once; limit the blast radius and confirm improvement after remediation using the same metrics.

In the diagram, the new version is first delivered to some users while the remaining users continue to receive the stable version. The team compares the error rate and latency for the same operations in both groups. If the problem is limited to the new version, it stops the rollout according to predefined conditions. If a rollback is required, it also limits the scope and confirms that business operations have recovered after the change using the same metrics.

sources.label: SAP-C03 Exam Guide: Observability and Automation

checkpoints.prompt: An engineer responsible for deploying common network settings across multiple accounts and Regions wants to prevent differences caused by manual work. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Each administrator configures settings arbitrarily in the console, and differences are checked only after an incident.
choices.explanation: This loses configuration reproducibility and change tracking.

choices.text: Manage the common settings as IaC and design the execution role, target accounts, Regions, dependencies, policy validation, and drift checks.
choices.explanation: This enables both reproducible deployments and governance.

choices.text: Embed secrets in plaintext in the template.
choices.explanation: This undermines secrets management and auditing.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for deploying a new version of a payment API to production wants to limit the impact of any issues. Which procedure is most appropriate?

choices.text: Do not record the artifact version and approval.
choices.explanation: This makes investigating the cause and rolling back difficult.

choices.text: Deploy to a limited scope, verify the predefined quality, latency, error-rate, and security results before expanding the deployment, and revert to a known-good version if an issue occurs.
choices.explanation: This allows the change's effects and impact to be observed while deploying safely.

choices.text: Deploy to all users simultaneously and investigate the cause if an issue occurs.
choices.explanation: The scope of the incident's impact will become larger.

checkpoints.prompt: Immediately after deploying a new version of the payment API to 5% of traffic as a canary, the error rate increased only for the canary. The known-good version and the same operation in other accounts are normal. Without attributing the cause solely to the alarm, which is the most appropriate way to respond while limiting the impact?

choices.text: Assume that the alarm alone is the cause and restart services in all Regions simultaneously.
choices.explanation: Changing everything without checking the differences between the canary and the known-good version or the change time risks mistaking correlation for causation and expanding the impact.

choices.text: Expand the canary traffic as it is, and delete the logs without checking the metrics after remediation.
choices.explanation: This ignores the condition that the anomaly is limited to the candidate version, expands the impact, and removes the evidence needed to compare causes and confirm whether remediation succeeded.

choices.text: Compare latency, errors, logs, and change times for the same operation between the canary and the known-good version, and stop expanding the traffic. Only if predefined conditions are met, perform a limited rollback of the canary with least privilege, then verify the result using the same metrics.
choices.explanation: This treats the differences between the canary and the healthy comparison target as evidence and tests the causal hypothesis. Only when the stop and limited-rollback conditions are met can the scope of the action be narrowed and the version rolled back, after which recovery can be confirmed with the same measurements.
